claims.text: Dermatology AI fails in dark-skin, non-cancer settings.
claims.poster_quote: Dermatology AI fails in dark-skin, non-cancer settings.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Patients present with more pigmented skin, and with a disease burden dominated by inflammatory and infectious conditions (eczema, tinea, impetigo, scabies) that are largely absent from cancer-centric training data.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that dermatology AI models trained on light-skinned, cancer-focused data fail in settings where patients have darker skin and non-cancerous conditions like eczema or tinea. This supports the claim.

claims.text: Disease shift may matter more than skin tone underrepresentation.
claims.poster_quote: Disease shift may matter more than skin tone underrepresentation.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Distribution shift dominates across all evaluated models.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that distribution shift dominates across all evaluated models, supporting the claim that disease shift may matter more than skin tone underrepresentation.

claims.text: Models trained on light-skinned, cancer-focused data are deployed where patients have darker skin and non-cancerous conditions like eczema or tinea.
claims.poster_quote: Models trained on light-skinned, cancer-focused data are deployed where patients have darker skin and non-cancerous conditions like eczema or tinea.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Dermatology artificial intelligence (AI) models are trained predominantly on light-skinned, cancer-focused image collections, yet are increasingly proposed for deployment in resource-constrained settings (RCS) whose patients differ from the training population along two confounded axes at once: skin tone and disease distribution.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that models trained on light-skinned, cancer-focused data are deployed in settings where patients have darker skin and non-cancerous conditions.

claims.text: Distribution shift causes bigger drops than tone gaps.
claims.poster_quote: Distribution shift causes bigger drops than tone gaps.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Distribution shift dominates across all evaluated models.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that distribution shift causes bigger drops in performance than tone gaps, supporting the claim.

claims.text: Cancer baseline on SCIN shows a drop in balanced accuracy from 0.62 to 0.21.
claims.poster_quote: Table 2 shows 0.62→0.21 drop for cancer baseline on SCIN.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: the cancer baseline degrades sharply from its in-domain performance to unfamiliar conditions (a drop from 0.62 to 0.21 balanced accuracy across clinical categories)
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that the cancer baseline shows a drop in balanced accuracy from 0.62 to 0.21 on SCIN.

claims.text: Label-free analysis reveals cancer features collapse to near-chance on unfamiliar conditions.
claims.poster_quote: Label-free analysis reveals cancer features collapse to near-chance on unfamiliar conditions (+0.06 purity lift).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On its home domain, the cancer baseline has the strongest representational structure of any model (purity lift +0.42), yet on SCIN its features barely separate conditions (+0.06) close to chance, demonstrating a genuine representational deficit rather than a missing output head.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that label-free analysis reveals that cancer features collapse to near-chance on unfamiliar conditions.

claims.text: Label-free analysis shows a +0.06 purity lift for cancer features on unfamiliar conditions.
claims.poster_quote: Label-free analysis reveals cancer features collapse to near-chance on unfamiliar conditions (+0.06 purity lift).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: On its home domain, the cancer baseline has the strongest representational structure of any model (purity lift +0.42), yet on SCIN its features barely separate conditions (+0.06) close to chance, demonstrating a genuine representational deficit rather than a missing output head.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that the label-free analysis shows a +0.06 purity lift for cancer features on unfamiliar conditions.

claims.text: Dermatology models retain transferable structure with a +0.23 purity lift.
claims.poster_quote: while dermatology models retain transferable structure (DermLIP +0.23).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Dermatology foundation models retain three to four times more transferable structure under the same unfamiliar conditions (DermLIP +0.23).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that dermatology models retain transferable structure with a +0.23 purity lift.

claims.text: Representation quality strongly correlates with recoverable performance (r=0.90).
claims.poster_quote: Representation quality strongly correlates with recoverable performance (r=0.90).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Across models, recoverable performance closely tracks the label-free representation quality of Fig. 2 (r = 0.90 between SCIN purity lift and full-probe balanced accuracy across the four models).
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that representation quality strongly correlates with recoverable performance (r=0.90).

claims.text: Dermatology foundation models should be used instead of cancer-trained models.
claims.poster_quote: Use dermatology foundation models, not cancer ones.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Our findings suggest tentative guidance for teams building dermatology AI under resource constraints. First, model selection may matter more than local retraining: since recoverable performance is bounded by representation quality, teams may benefit from starting with a dermatology-pretrained foundation model rather than a cancer-specialized classifier.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly recommends using dermatology foundation models instead of cancer-trained models for better performance in resource-constrained settings.

claims.text: Adaptation with 10 examples per class is possible.
